newsitem.title: USA: Bonneville offers Wed peak firm, non-firm power.
newsitem.headline: Bonneville offers Wed peak firm, non-firm power.

text.p: Bonneville Power Administration (BPA) expanded next-day offers of surplus power to include up to 200 megawatts (MW) firm on-peak power and up to 500 MW of non-firm, the federal agency said Tuesday.
BPA also offered unlimited volumes of off-peak power for both firm and non-firm sales, compared with respective limits of 500 MW and 300 MW for Tuesday pre-schedulings.
Wednesday firm off-peak prices were lowered to $17.00 per megawatt hour (MWh) from $20.00 for both Northwest and California-Oregon border (COB) deliveries.
Firm on-peak power (hours ending 0600-2200 PST) was offered at $22.25 per MWh for Northwest deliveries and $23.00 for COB.

Prices for non-firm power during hours ending 0100-0500 and 2400 PST on Tuesday were also $3.00 lower at $17.50 per MWh. Non-firm prices for hours ending 0600 and 2300 were dropped by $4.00 to $20.00.
Wednesday non-firm power during peak demand hours was offered at $22.50 in the Northwest and at $23.50 for COB.
